title: Article 217 — Appointment and conditions of the office of a Judge of a High Court

content.overview: Article 217 provides that every Judge of a High Court shall be appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, the Governor of the State, and, in the case of appointment of a Judge other than the Chief Justice, the Chief Justice of the High Court. A Judge holds office until the age of sixty-two years (subject to resignation, removal under Art 218/124 process, or appointment to the Supreme Court). Qualifications and other conditions (citizenship, judicial office or advocacy experience, oath, etc.) are set out in the article.
content.glance: HC Judge appointed by President after consultation (CJI, Governor, HC CJ for non-CJ appointments). Tenure until 62. Qualifications: citizen; 10 years judicial office or 10 years HC advocacy (as specified).
content.study:
Article 217:
(1) Appointment by President after consultation with CJI, Governor of the State, and (for non-CJ) the Chief Justice of the High Court. Practice is governed by the collegium system as developed by the Supreme Court.
(2) Tenure until age 62; earlier termination by resignation, removal (address under Art 218 read with Art 124 procedure), or SC appointment.
(3)–(4) Qualifications: citizen of India; held judicial office in India for 10 years, or been an advocate of a High Court (or of two or more such Courts in succession) for 10 years, with related computation rules.

Examination: appointment consultations; age 62; qualifications; removal pathway via Art 218/124.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Appointment by President after consultation with CJI, Governor, and (for non-CJ) HC Chief Justice.
2. Holds office until 62 (unless resigns, removed, or appointed to SC).
3. Qualifications: citizen; 10 years judicial office or 10 years advocacy in HC(s) as specified.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How is a High Court Judge appointed under Article 217?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 217, every Judge of a High Court is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, the Governor of the State, and, in the case of a Judge other than the Chief Justice, the Chief Justice of the High Court. A Judge holds office until the age of sixty-two years, subject to resignation, removal, or appointment to the Supreme Court. Qualifications include citizenship and either ten years’ judicial office in India or ten years’ advocacy in a High Court (or successive High Courts) as provided in the article.
